title: Greenhouse effect

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Conservation of energy
items.clue: It cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred.

items.label: Albedo (α)
items.clue: The fraction of incident radiation that a planet or surface scatters back.

items.label: Emissivity (e)
items.clue: The ratio of the power radiated per unit area to that of an ideal black surface at the same temperature.

items.label: Greenhouse effect
items.clue: The warming of a planet's surface above the temperature it would have if its atmosphere did not absorb infrared radiation.

questions.stem: In a simple model of Earth's global mean energy flows, 340 W m⁻² of solar radiation arrives at the top of the atmosphere and 100 W m⁻² of this is scattered back to space by clouds, air and the surface. The surface emits 390 W m⁻² of infrared radiation. Earth is in energy equilibrium. What intensity of infrared radiation leaves Earth at the top of the atmosphere?

options.text: 340 W m⁻²
100 W m⁻²
390 W m⁻²
240 W m⁻²

questions.stem: Which statement about the emissivity of a surface is correct?

options.text: It compares the power radiated per unit area with that of a black body at the same temperature.
It is the power radiated per unit area of the surface, so it is measured in watts per square metre.
It is the fraction of the incident radiation that the surface reflects, so it is equal to its albedo.
It depends on the visible colour of a surface, so white snow has an emissivity close to zero.

questions.explanation: Emissivity = (power radiated per unit area)/σT⁴, where σT⁴ is the power per unit area radiated by an ideal black surface at the same temperature. It is a ratio with no unit, between 0 and 1.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the albedo of a planet?

options.text: The total power absorbed by the planet divided by the total power incident on it
The total power scattered by the planet divided by the total power incident on it
The power reflected by each square metre of the planet's surface, in W m⁻²
The infrared power the planet emits divided by the power incident on it

questions.explanation: Albedo = total scattered power / total incident power. It is a ratio with no unit; Earth's mean value is about 0.30.

questions.stem: Satellite measurements show that the mean albedo of the polar regions is much higher than that of the tropical oceans. Which is the best explanation?

options.text: Snow and ice cover much of the surface, and low-angle sunlight is reflected more strongly.
Snow and ice reflect all of the sunlight that falls on them, whereas ocean water reflects none of it.
The polar regions are further from the Sun, so more of the sunlight that reaches them is reflected.
The polar surfaces are colder, and colder surfaces reflect a larger fraction of the radiation on them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solar constant?

options.text: The intensity of the Sun's radiation on a horizontal surface at ground level, averaged over a whole year at the equator
The total power emitted by the Sun in all directions, which stays constant from one year to the next
The intensity of sunlight above the atmosphere, on a surface perpendicular to the rays, at the mean Earth–Sun distance
The mean intensity of the Sun's radiation averaged over the whole of Earth's spherical surface, day and night

questions.explanation: This is the definition. S ≈ 1.36 × 10³ W m⁻². It is measured by satellites above the atmosphere, on a surface facing the Sun, at the mean distance of Earth from the Sun.

questions.stem: The mean intensity of solar radiation incident on a planet's whole surface is S/4, where S is the solar constant. What is the origin of the factor of 4?

options.text: Half of the surface is in darkness at any instant, and half of the sunlight reaching the day side is reflected.
The atmosphere absorbs or scatters three quarters of the Sun's radiation before it can reach the surface.
The planet intercepts power over its cross-section πR², but this power is spread over its total surface area 4πR².
The Sun's radiation spreads out over a sphere of area 4πd², so only a quarter of it reaches the planet.

questions.stem: Which statement about the main greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere is correct?

options.text: Each of them has natural sources as well as sources in human activity.
Water vapour is not one of them, since it comes only from natural evaporation.
Nitrogen and oxygen are the main ones, as they make up about 99% of dry air.
They are all pollutants produced only by industry, transport and farming.

questions.explanation: Methane, water vapour, carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide all have natural origins (wetlands for CH₄, evaporation for H₂O, respiration and volcanoes for CO₂, soil bacteria for N₂O) and origins in human activity (livestock, irrigation, burning fossil fuels, nitrogen fertilisers).

questions.stem: A carbon dioxide molecule in the atmosphere absorbs an infrared photon emitted by Earth's surface. What happens?

options.text: It reflects the photon, so that the infrared radiation is sent straight back down towards the Earth's surface.
It moves to a higher vibrational energy level, and the energy is later emitted as infrared in all directions.
It moves to a higher energy level and then emits the infrared downwards, back to the surface.
It splits into atoms, because the photon's energy is enough to break the molecule's bonds.

questions.explanation: The photon energy matches the spacing of the molecule's vibrational energy levels, so the molecule is excited. The energy is later emitted as infrared (often after being shared in collisions) with no preferred direction, so part returns towards the surface and part goes upwards.

questions.stem: According to the resonance model, how do greenhouse-gas molecules absorb infrared radiation?

options.text: Radiation whose frequency equals a natural frequency of vibration of the bonds drives large vibrations.
Infrared photons carry more energy than visible ones, so they shake the molecules more violently.
The molecules vibrate at whatever frequency the radiation has, so all are absorbed equally.
Radiation at a natural frequency of the bonds makes them vibrate until they break, releasing the energy.

questions.explanation: In the resonance model the bonds act like springs with natural frequencies. Infrared at a natural frequency drives the vibration at resonance, the amplitude grows, and energy is absorbed strongly; at other frequencies little is absorbed.

questions.stem: What is meant by the enhanced greenhouse effect?

options.text: The greenhouse effect itself, which would not occur at all without the greenhouse gases released by human activity
Extra warming caused by holes in the ozone layer, which let more solar radiation through to the ground
Direct warming of the air by the heat released when fuels are burned in engines and power stations
The augmentation of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities that add greenhouse gases to the air

questions.explanation: This matches the guide: the augmentation of the greenhouse effect due to human activities, which raise the concentrations of greenhouse gases, chiefly by burning fossil fuels.

questions.stem: A simple model of Earth uses a solar constant of 1.36 × 10³ W m⁻² and an albedo of 0.30. The atmosphere absorbs none of the incoming solar radiation. The atmosphere, at a temperature of 242 K and with emissivity 0.780, radiates an intensity eσT⁴ upwards to space and an equal intensity downwards to the surface. The surface is a black body. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, what is the equilibrium temperature of the surface?

A planet orbits a star at a distance where the intensity of the star's radiation, the equivalent of the solar constant, is 2.40 × 10³ W m⁻². The planet's albedo is 0.40 and its emissivity is 0.80. Using σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W m⁻² K⁻⁴, estimate the planet's equilibrium temperature.
questions.explanation: (1 − α)S/4 = eσT⁴: 0.60 × 600 = 360 W m⁻² = 0.80 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × T⁴, so T = 298 K. The emissivity below 1 means the planet must be warmer than a black body to radiate the same intensity.
